messages.subject: spec() function x-axis calculation
parts:
Hi there,

I was wondering if someone could explain why the x-axis calculation for the spectrum in the spec() function:

    x <- seq(0, (f/2) - (f/wl), length.out = n%/%2)/1000

includes the f/wl term.  I saw from Arvind Sowmyan's previous thread that there was a small bug with the definition of wl when from and to are specified.  But I'm still not quite sure why there is this f/wl term.  If there were just the f/2 term, that makes sense to me because that would be the Nyquist frequency.  How does the f/wl term come in?  I apologize for the naive question---I'm pretty inexperienced with DSP.

Thank you very much,
Kristine

Dear Kristine,

f/2 is the Nyquist frequency.
f/wl is the frequency resolution of the FFT or the bin width of the FFT. If you have a 44100 Hz sampling frequency and that you set up the length of the FFT window (wl) at 512 samples, the spectrum will have a frequency resolution of f/wl = 86.13 Hz. A spectrum is usually drawn with lines as it was continuous but it should actually plotted as a barplot.
The x-axis of the spec() and meanspec() ends at the Nyquist frequency - 1 spectrum bin, this is to avoid the Nyquist frequency, just be one step below.
HTH
Jerome
